_readme: Narration delivery for the pilot (generate_story_audio.py). Settled by ear 2026-08: the plain voice at 128k mp3 with no speed adjustment and no emotion sounded clean, while 96k / a speed adjustment / the emotion parameter (in some combination) made it nasal and watery — so those stay off until re-tested one at a time with --diagnose. Sentence pauses at 250ms were picked from --pause-test. Resolution order for every setting is age_bands > tellers > top level, so a band can override pace or even voice while tellers still choose who is telling. Every band the library may contain has an entry, including 3-4 and 11-12 which have no stories yet — otherwise a new band would silently inherit the 9-10 pacing. Younger bands get longer pauses rather than slower speech, because pauses cost nothing in audio quality and a speed adjustment is exactly what we suspect of the artifacts — revisit with `--diagnose` at 128k before adding speed back. Paragraph and segment gaps are NOT here: they're player-side (BujuPilot.narration in pilot/js/stories.js) and are themselves scaled per age band, so they retune without regenerating. Anything in this file is baked into the mp3s: change it and regenerate with --force. 2026-08 update: the 3-4 band was the first to be voiced and the first listened to by a parent, and it came back 'too fast and too harsh'. The cause was that younger bands only ever got longer PAUSES — every word was still delivered at speed 1.0 — so a three-year-old's story was fast bursts separated by 550ms of silence, which reads as staccato rather than gentle. 3-4 now slows the words (speed 0.92) and shortens the gaps to 400ms so it flows instead of stuttering. 0.85 was tried first and was audibly nasal, confirming the long-standing suspicion about this knob: sonic-3's speed adjustment degrades the voice, and the degradation scales with how far from 1.0 you push it. Treat speed as a small trim, not as the way to get a gentle read — for that, pick a voice that is natively slow and warm and leave speed alone. If the words sound watery at 0.85, that is the artifact this file has always suspected of the speed knob: back off toward 0.9 and re-check with --diagnose at 128k rather than reverting to 1.0. LANGUAGES (2026-08): `languages` maps a language code to the voice that reads it. Resolution for voice_id is languages > age_bands > tellers > top level — a story narrated in Hindi uses the Hindi voice whatever its teller says, because teller is about who is telling, not what language they speak. Pace still resolves by band. English is listed explicitly so the default is visible rather than implied. A language here is only half the job: the story also needs a `translations.<lang>` block, or there is nothing for the voice to read — a voice does not translate. 2026-08-14: the whole library had been narrated by one young-sounding voice, which reads as a peer to a 5-year-old and as someone YOUNGER than the listener at 11-12 — a credibility problem for the oldest band, which is four of the eight pilot families. 11-12 English now uses f039066f-cdb7-45ed-b51d-1034ae2f04a0, a gentle adult woman, picked by ear from five candidates (d2c66146 / f28bff4a / f6a11db5 / 1203e44b / 56b87df1 were all rejected before anything was generated with them). Note what the answer turned out NOT to be: the problem was never that the narrator was female, it was that she sounded like a peer rather than an adult reading to you. An older-sounding woman fixes it; an old man was tried and was worse. Note the new resolution slot that makes this possible: `age_bands.<band>.languages.<lang>` is checked BEFORE the top-level `languages`, because `languages.en.voice_id` would otherwise shadow every band-level voice override for English. Read it as 'for this band, in this language, use this voice'. Hindi is untouched — it has no band entry, so it still falls through to `languages.hi`. 2026-09-04: the 5-6 band came back 'a bit fast, and the periods feel long' on stories written in short bursts (The Great Orange Sunset Machine: 56% of sentences under 25 chars). Same medicine as 3-4 — slow the words a little, shorten the gaps — plus a new rule: a sentence shorter than `short_sentence_chars` is followed by `short_sentence_pause_ms` instead of the full pause, so a run of 'No orange. Only red. Only yellow.' keeps its rhythm instead of stalling three times. Picked by ear with scripts/pace_test.py from (1.0/400 reference, 0.95/300, 0.92/300, 0.92/300/short 25->200); 0.95/300/short 25->200 is what shipped. Both short_* keys resolve like every other setting and are baked into the mp3s; api/pilot-name-audio.js mirrors the rule from the values stamped into stories.json.
